newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan prices seen steady on falling stocks.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan prices seen steady on falling stocks.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures prices are expected to be steady to firmer this week, supported by fading worries over a possible supply surplus in the near-term due to falling domestic inventories, traders said on Monday.
Higher offer prices for Thai benchmark rubber to Japan may also provide support, the traders said.
One concern, however, is the currency market, where renewed gains by the yen against the dollar could pour cold water on sentiment, which appears to be improving slightly, they said.
"The rubber market environment looks better due to factors such as decreasing domestic rubber stocks and firmer Thai offer prices to Japan," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
"Unless the yen continues to climb, rubber prices are likely to be a tad firmer this week," he said.
A stronger yen against the dollar pushes down the price of imports into Japan.
The benchmark October contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the Monday morning session at 143.3 yen, compared with 143.9 yen last Friday.
Benchmark October on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 144.0 yen at the end of the second trading session, up from Friday's 143.9 yen close.
Japanese rubber stocks as of May 10 amounted to 37,182 tonnes, down by 2,407 tonnes at the end of April, according to the Rubber Trade Association of Japan.
"The falling trend in Japan's rubber stocks is likely to continue until the end of June," the analyst said. "Stocks may decrease to around 30,000 tonnes," he said.
Thai rubber to Japan was offered at 120 U.S. cents per kg on a FOB basis on Monday, against 110 U.S. cents as of May 12.

Traders said one of the reasons for the rise could be the expected start of the Thai government's new intervention policy at the higher intervention price of 29 baht per kg, compared with 27.50 baht previously.

"There is talk that supplies of Ribbed Smoked Sheet (RSS3) grade rubber in producing countries have been tighter, due mainly to expectations that the Thai government will start its new intervention policy," a trader said.
It is not clear when the new purchasing programme will start, traders said.
A technical analyst at another commodity broker said he expected the TOCOM benchmark October futures contract to try the upside at 145 yen this week.
"Technically, the key is whether the TOCOM benchmark will be able to break above the 145 yen level. If it does, more gains are possible," the analyst said.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 157 yen on Monday, against 151 yen on May 12.
